voices.note: anonymous redactorial voice: the אילימא answer, אמרי (35b.14), the objections, the אלא at 35b.18 and its defences
the mishnah cited והתנן at 35b.16: one who vows from food is permitted water and salt

props.gloss_en: entertained: [wine has its own blessing] because it changed for the better, therefore its blessing changed
over olive oil one blesses 'who creates the fruit of the tree'
there [oil kept its blessing] because it is impossible [to change it]: how would we bless? 'who creates the fruit of the olive'? -- the fruit itself is called olive
Mar Zutra: [oil changed for the better yet kept its blessing, unlike wine, because] wine nourishes and oil does not nourish
the mishnah: one who vows [to abstain] from food is permitted water and salt
and we discussed it: water and salt are what is not called food -- so everything else is called food
Rav and Shmuel: one blesses 'who creates kinds of food' only over the five species alone
Rav Huna: [the mishnah speaks] of one who says 'whatever nourishes is [forbidden] to me'
rather: [oil changed for the better yet kept its blessing, unlike wine, because] wine satisfies and oil does not satisfy
Rava would drink wine all of Passover eve, so that it would whet his appetite and he would eat more matza
it is written: 'wine gladdens the heart of man ... and bread sustains man's heart' (Ps 104:15) -- bread is what satisfies; wine does not satisfy
people do not make their meal on it [so the three blessings after a meal are not said over wine]
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak to Rava: if one made his meal on it, what [is the law]?
Rava: when Elijah comes and says whether it is a fixed meal [we shall know]; now, at any rate, his intention is void against [that of] all people

supports.gloss_en: אלמא משחא זיין -- since the vow 'whatever nourishes' leaves only water and salt permitted, oil is among what nourishes

objections.gloss_en: והרי שמן, דאשתני לעילויא ולא אשתני לברכה -- oil too changed for the better, yet its blessing did not change

answered_by.gloss_en: אמרי: התם משום דלא אפשר -- oil kept its blessing only because no fitting formula exists (= p_hatam_lo_efshar; refuted at 35b.15 by ונבריך עליה בורא פרי עץ זית and displaced by אלא)
אלא אמר מר זוטרא: חמרא זיין, משחא לא זיין -- wine nourishes, oil does not (= p_mar_zutra_zayin; refuted at 35b.16-18, אלמא משחא זיין, and displaced by אלא)
אלא: חמרא סעיד, ומשחא לא סעיד -- wine satisfies, oil does not (= p_chamra_saeid; survives the difficulties of 35b.18-20)

objections.gloss_en: ונבריך עליה בורא פרי עץ זית! -- a fitting formula does exist, 'who creates the fruit of the olive tree', so impossibility is not the reason

ומשחא לא זיין? והתנן: הנודר מן המזון מותר במים ובמלח -- everything but water and salt is called food; and on Rav Huna's okimta (the vow was 'whatever nourishes') it follows: אלמא משחא זיין (35b.18). Unanswered: the stam moves to a further answer with אלא
נימא תיהוי תיובתא דרב ושמואל -- if everything but water and salt is 'food', then 'food' is not confined to the five species

answered_by.gloss_en: באומר כל הזן עלי -- the vow was 'whatever nourishes', which is wider than 'food' (= p_rav_huna_kol_hazan)

objections.gloss_en: וחמרא מי סעיד? והא רבא הוה שתי חמרא כל מעלי יומא דפסחא כי היכי דנגרריה ללביה -- wine whets the appetite rather than satisfying

answered_by.gloss_en: טובא גריר, פורתא סעיד -- much whets, a little satisfies

objections.gloss_en: ומי סעיד כלל? והכתיב ...ולחם לבב אנוש יסעד -- bread is what satisfies, wine does not (a verse; no ObjectionKind names one)

answered_by.gloss_en: אלא, חמרא אית ביה תרתי: סעיד ומשמח; נהמא מסעד סעיד, שמוחי לא משמח -- wine both satisfies and gladdens; bread only satisfies, so the verse assigns bread satisfying and wine gladdening

objections.gloss_en: אי הכי נבריך עליה שלש ברכות! -- if wine satisfies, let the three blessings [after a meal] be said over it

answered_by.gloss_en: לא קבעי אינשי סעודתייהו עלויה -- people do not make their meal on it (= p_lo_kavei_inshei)
